{"actions": [], "mode": "answer", "reply": "I cannot fix these problems with the parts listed. I will not apply a misleading swap.

The main actuator is the limiting factor. The MG996R stalls at 11.01 kg·cm, but the loads need 22.0 kg·cm at the pelvis, 26.6 kg·cm at the torso shell, 31.6 kg·cm at the shoulder yoke, 44.3 kg·cm at the left upper arm, 112.7 kg·cm at the left thigh, and 173.9 kg·cm at the torso core. The strongest listed alternative is the DS3218 at 21.5 kg·cm. That still fails every one of those, including the pelvis at 22.0 kg·cm, and is about 8× too weak for the 173.9 kg·cm torso core.

The left hip yaw is similar. It needs 114.8 kg·cm and the CubeMars AK60-6 stalls at 91.74 kg·cm. Every listed hobby-servo replacement is weaker than that, at 21.5 kg·cm or less.

Power also cannot be fixed from the list. Peak current is 17.9 A and the present supply is delivering about 0 A. No listed supply option is rated to cover 17.9 A at the required 48 V, 24 V and 12 V actuator voltages.

This needs stronger actuators outside the listed options, a shorter lever arm / lighter structure, or both, plus a supply rated above 17.9 A. The waist yaw at 96 % and waist pitch at 75 % of stall torque would also remain hot and over-worn."}
